headline: Scientists Map 51 Solutions That Could Trigger Unstoppable Planetary Healing
meta_description: Researchers have identified 51 ready-to-implement environmental solutions that could rapidly repair the planet within five years if scaled globally.
summary_short: Academics have identified 51 environmental solutions that could trigger an unstoppable wave of positive change across forests, oceans, energy and more.
body:
Scientists from the University of Exeter's Green Futures Solutions team and the Earthshot Prize have identified 51 environmental solutions capable of triggering what researchers describe as an "unstoppable" wave of positive change. The breakthrough lies in reversing how we think about tipping points: rather than focusing on ecosystem collapse, researchers are studying positive tipping points—moments when one success sparks a cascade of others. Many solutions already exist somewhere in the world and could rapidly repair the planet within five years if scaled up with adequate support. Some, like electric vehicle adoption in Norway and global solar expansion, have already reached stabilisation, while others are still accelerating.

The solutions span diverse challenges. Deforestation-free sourcing standards could restructure economic incentives for millions of agricultural producers, since cattle, soy, timber and cocoa account for around 70% of tropical forest loss. In health, clean cooking and heating alternatives could cut harmful emissions by 80%, benefiting the two billion people still relying on polluting systems. Marine protected areas show similar promise—once fish populations recover in protected zones and spill into fished waters, fishers themselves become advocates for more protection, creating self-expanding networks. On packaging, Notpla, the 2022 Earthshot Prize winner, has already replaced more than 32 million units of single-use plastic with seaweed-based materials in just three years.

The research builds on a simple insight: the world's most pressing problems aren't unsolvable—they're just waiting for coordinated action. From Form Energy's breakthrough iron-air batteries to d.light's solar systems across Africa and India, proven solutions exist. What's needed now is the will and support to scale them globally.

Cattle, soy, timber and cocoa drive 70% of tropical forest loss
Notpla replaced 32 million single-use plastic units with seaweed in three years
Two billion people still use polluting cooking and heating systems
Solutions could repair planet within five years if scaled
